summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of primary sclerosing cholangitis (PSC) complicated by cirrhosis was admitted with right upper quadrant abdominal pain and fever, concerning for recurrent cholangitis. She was started on intravenous meropenem, with improvement in symptoms and liver enzymes. An ERCP was performed, which showed no treatable strictures or stones, though a biliary biopsy was obtained. A PICC line was placed to complete a five-day course of ertapenem at home. Her diarrhea was evaluated and found to be C. difficile negative, likely due to recent antibiotics. She was discharged on a plan to transition to rifaximin after finishing IV therapy, with instructions to follow up with gastroenterology and schedule a colonoscopy. Her chronic conditions, including hypertension and hypothyroidism, were managed, and she returned to baseline function.
